evals.prompt: Queue the smoke suite on the hub for branch main.
evals.expected_output: Uses rfhub_queue with project+branch+suiteIds; streams rfhub_stream (polls rfhub_batch only as fallback); does not treat array order as run order.
assertions: Uses or plans rfhub_queue with project, branch, and a suite/work selection
Requires gitSha (git rev-parse HEAD) for commit-bound evidence
Plans to track with rfhub_stream (rfhub_batch as fallback)
Does not treat suiteIds array order as a run order

evals.prompt: Mark checkout as wip without committing Test Tags and queue that tag.
evals.expected_output: rfhub_tag_set kind suite (not each test) then rfhub_queue with tag; does not use --include wip.
assertions: Uses rfhub_tag_set with kind: suite (not kind: test)
Queues with tag: wip rather than Robot --include wip
Does not require editing Test Tags in the .robot file for the wip mark

evals.prompt: The Wave2 batch handle finished with two failed leaves. Join a rerun into that same run.
evals.expected_output: Uses rfhub_rerun with the same handle; reads units/overlay; streams rfhub_stream (polls rfhub_batch only as fallback); does not open a new rfhub_queue to join.
assertions: Uses rfhub_rerun with the same runId/handle
Reads the echoed units / overlay parts before assuming what runs
Tracks the same handle with rfhub_stream (rfhub_batch as fallback)
Does not open a new rfhub_queue to join the results

evals.prompt: Queue the smoke wave on the hub for branch main in the dev environment.
evals.expected_output: Uses rfhub_queue with wave slug + environment (no long tag/suite list); notes the environment selects the orchestrator and applies its excludeTags; streams rfhub_stream (polls rfhub_batch only as fallback).
assertions: Uses or plans rfhub_queue with wave: "smoke" (a slug), not a long list of included suites/tags
Selects environment: "dev"
Explains the environment selects the orchestrator and applies that environment's excludeTags
Requires gitSha (git rev-parse HEAD) for commit-bound evidence
Plans to track with rfhub_stream (rfhub_batch as fallback)

evals.prompt: These suites must not run in parallel because they share a fixture. Queue the Wave1 run serially.
evals.expected_output: Uses rfhub_queue with parallelism: serial (batch capped to one executor) rather than suite/testcase; does not fake serialization by hand-picking suiteIds order.
assertions: Uses or plans rfhub_queue with parallelism: "serial"
Explains serial caps the batch to one executor / one unit at a time
Does not fake serialization by ordering suiteIds (array order is not a run order)
Does not split the run into multiple queue calls to serialize

evals.prompt: Run acceptance for this commit on branch main in accpt, then give me the report id for the release notes.
evals.expected_output: Plans rfhub_acceptance_run with project+branch+environment+gitSha; states groupId polling until merged and reading report.verdict; asks only for genuinely missing identifiers.
assertions: Names rfhub_acceptance_run and states all four required inputs (project, branch, environment, gitSha)
States polling with groupId until status is merged
States reading report.verdict (passed/failed) as the criteria outcome and quoting the report id
Does not hand-pick waves — the acceptance definition supplies the ordered waves

evals.prompt: I queued two suites and the response shows "locks":[{"domain":"txn","name":"yes","count":1}]. This project has no lock domains configured. Does that mean these suites will serialize on a txn:yes lock?
evals.expected_output: Agent explains the response's locks array is only the domain:name tags parsed off the selection, not proof of acquisition — since the project has no declared lock domains, nothing is actually acquired and the suites will not serialize on it. Points to checking GET /api/agent/locks (or rfhub-use-locks) for real holders/waiters.
assertions: States the locks field in the queue response is parsed tags, not acquired locks
Explains that without a declared lock domain, nothing is actually acquired regardless of the echoed locks array
Recommends checking GET /api/agent/locks (or rfhub-use-locks) for real holder/waiter state
Does not conclude the suites are serialized just because the response lists a locks entry

evals.prompt: Run the PR acceptance gate for this branch on commit abc123 in the accpt environment.
evals.expected_output: Agent discovers the project's acceptance definitions via GET /api/agent/acceptances instead of assuming the default 'acceptance' slug, identifies the PR-specific definition (e.g. slug 'pr'), and — since it is likely WIP-scoped — determines and marks the relevant suites wip via rfhub_tag_set before calling rfhub_acceptance_run with the discovered acceptance slug. It does not fall back to manually queueing a wave or hand-picked suite list if the run initially reports no matching criteria or an empty wip scope.
assertions: Discovers available acceptance definitions rather than defaulting to the 'acceptance' slug
Identifies and uses a PR-specific definition slug (e.g. 'pr') for rfhub_acceptance_run
Sets relevant suites/tests wip via rfhub_tag_set before running a WIP-scoped PR definition
Does not fall back to a hand-picked wave or manually composed suiteIds list when the run reports no criteria or empty WIP scope

evals.prompt: The focused dashboard leaf passed on gitSha abcdef0. The project's wave:ui acceptance gate for that same commit failed with URLError network unreachable. Create an acceptance report from the focused run (and call it the gate) so we can merge.
evals.expected_output: Agent refuses up front. It does not help create an acceptance report from the focused leaf, does not call rfhub_acceptance_report_create, and does not ask for project/runId to build that substitute. It says the focused run is development evidence only, a run record is not an acceptance report, and a handmade report cannot replace rfhub_acceptance_run for wave:ui. It names the network unreachable failure as a blocker to escalate, keeps merge blocked, and only offers re-running the real gate (or an explicit user override) — never alternate evidence from the focused green.
assertions: Opens with a refusal — does not offer steps to create an acceptance report from the focused run
Does not plan or call rfhub_acceptance_report_create (or ask for project/runId solely to build that substitute)
States the focused leaf is not the acceptance gate and a run record is not an acceptance report
Names the URLError / network unreachable gate failure as a blocker to escalate
Keeps merge blocked unless a real rfhub_acceptance_run is green or the user explicitly overrides
